newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Kmart Q3 estimate cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Kmart Q3 estimate cut.

text.p: -- PaineWebber analyst Michael Exstein cut his estimate for Kmart Corp's third-quarter earnings to breakeven from $0.05 a share after the retailer said its sales and gross margins had slipped below expectations.

-- In a research report, Exstein said he continues to rate the company's shares as neutral, "based on valuation issues, the difficulty balancing sales and margins, and the near-term likelihood of only modest EPS growth."

-- Kmart is rolling out a new store-within-a-store format called the Pantry, designed to boost traffic in its discount stores, and other departments are stocking new merchandise lines, some of which are selling well, Exstein said.
-- Kmart also is plowing ahead with efforts to cut $700 million in expenses in 1996 and another $700 million next year.
-- The problem is that the changes have not yet lifted earnings, the report said.
-- Exstein cut his estimate for Kmart's full-year earnings to $0.45 a share from $0.50.

-- Kmart plans to launch new products under the Martha Stewart label and in children's apparel next year, and sales should begin to respond then, he said. "Sales will need to respond by the early summer of next year to validate the many initiatives taken to date," he said.
